label: Lord: dominion versus causing the being of and governing all else, with or without benevolence
resolution: The Dei Filius attributes (lord conjunct) and the bridge 'Whatever causes the being of everything else is LORD_1 of everything else' use LORD_1, the primitive Primitives.IsLord (dominion: authority to dispose of what is subject to one). LORD_2 (IsLordByCauseAndGovernment) types the two grounds q.13 a.7 and q.103 give for it: causing the being of everything else and governing everything else. They differ in content, not only in strength: LORD_2 is a matter of causal and directive power, LORD_1 of authority; neither is defined from the other and they are not identified. One statement relates them: the open sense bridge 'Whatever is LORD_2 is LORD_1'. Only an argument that lists it in sense_bridges passes from LORD_2 to LORD_1 (the routes nineGiveDeiFiliusLordBlessedTyped and deiFiliusRootLordBlessedTyped); the controls of DeiFiliusLordBlessed show that without it a being with the nine can be LORD_2 and not LORD_1. LORD_3 (IsBenevolentLordByCauseAndGovernment, #1733) is LORD_2 plus a separate conjunct: the being wills some good of its own to every other intellectual being in act as to being (recipient-directed willing). LORD_3 is stronger in content than LORD_2 and, like it, types grounds of dominion, not authority. Its only passage to LORD_1 is the open sense bridge 'Whatever is LORD_3 is LORD_1', strictly weaker than 'Whatever is LORD_2 is LORD_1' (DeiFiliusBenevolentLord Control.Controls part 2); only the route deiFiliusRootUnifiedBenevolentLord lists it in sense_bridges, and the controls show that without it a being can be LORD_3 and not LORD_1 (part 3).
